scenarios.title: Stop intake without losing the tail
scenarios.summary: Skip individual records, finish at a marker and pass unread data to the next stage.
scenarios.objective: Read the supplied standard-input stream one whole line at a time. Skip empty lines, lines starting with #, and any line starting off:. END alone ends intake. Accept on: followed by at least one character; print “Accepted: LINE” for each accepted whole line, preserving all text. Other pre-END lines print “Skipped invalid record: LINE” on stderr; keep processing. After intake print “Accepted count: N” and “Remaining input:” on separate lines, then copy the unread tail exactly. If END is found with no earlier invalid rows, return 0; otherwise return 1. If END is missing, add “Missing END marker.” on stderr and return 2, overriding 1. Messages end in a newline; only the forwarded tail keeps its original endings. source.txt is an audit copy of the supplied stream: preserve it and every other file.

scenarios.explanation:
Follow the assignment’s policy at each boundary, then report the combined result. The reference below is one supported solution; equivalent behavior is accepted.

One supported solution, available on request:
count=0
status=0
found=no
while IFS= read -r line || test -n "$line"; do
  case "$line" in
    ''|'#'*|off:*) continue ;;
    END) found=yes; break ;;
    on:?*) true ;;
    *) printf 'Skipped invalid record: %s\n' "$line" >&2; status=1; continue ;;
  esac
  printf 'Accepted: %s\n' "$line"
  count=$((count + 1))
done
if test "$found" = no; then
  printf 'Missing END marker.\n' >&2
  status=2
fi
printf 'Accepted count: %s\nRemaining input:\n' "$count"
cat
exit "$status"
hints: Handle ignored rows with continue before the common accepted-record printer. Handle END with break, not exit.
Read with IFS= read -r line || test -n "$line". Only the marker consumes END; following data must remain unread until cat.
Track accepted count, a found-marker flag and an overall status separately. Missing END has the stated error priority.
scenarios.simplifications: All files, standard input and execution are simulated offline. No host commands/files/network or real timing. break/continue are portable shell concepts; this simulator supports only own-scope for/while loops, optional canonical ASCII counts 1–24, and no loop transfer through pipeline stages or caller functions/captures. Unimplemented syntax is an honest diagnostic. Flat UTF-8 virtual files only, bounded instructions/output/memory. No real locks, atomic rename, concurrent writers or crash recovery.

teaching.prerequisite_note: Revisit line-preserving reads, case patterns, counters and exit status in the named prerequisites. This unit introduces skipping the current iteration and stopping a loop without ending the script. The example is separate, ungraded practice; your assignment draft is preserved.

concepts.title: Skip this item, keep the loop
concepts.text: continue stops the remaining commands in the current iteration. The loop then asks for its next item. In the example, skip is ignored without ending the selection.

concepts.title: Stop this loop, keep the script
concepts.text: break leaves the nearest active loop. Commands after done still run. exit ends the whole script instead, so it would lose the summary and the remaining-input handoff.

concepts.title: Read one whole record
concepts.text: The assignment receives finite standard input. IFS= read -r line preserves spaces and backslashes; || test -n "$line" keeps a final line without a line break. This was taught in Keep every label while reading text.

concepts.title: Recognize only the stated records
concepts.text: A case matches the whole line. on:?* requires on: followed by at least one character. Empty, # at the first character and off: records are skipped. Leading spaces are data, not silently trimmed.

concepts.title: Keep the tail for the next stage
concepts.text: Read only as far as END. After leaving the loop, cat copies whatever standard input has not yet been read, including its final line-break choice. Reading everything in advance would consume that tail.

concepts.title: Keep a useful overall result
concepts.text: Count accepted records, warn and continue after invalid pre-marker records, then report status 1. If END never arrives, report the separate missing-marker error/status 2. Ordinary completion is 0; later reporting commands must not erase that decision.

teaching.example:
for exhibit in lamp skip frame stop vase; do
  case "$exhibit" in
    skip) continue ;;
    stop) break ;;
  esac
  printf 'Kept: %s\n' "$exhibit"
done
teaching.inputs: The example creates its exhibit list itself; it has no arguments or input. gallery-notes.txt is separate practice data and stays unchanged. The assignment instead receives a line stream and source.txt audit copy.
teaching.try_change: Move stop to the front of the exhibit list and Run example. Nothing should be kept. Restore the original list to repair the example.

scenarios.retry_guidance: If the summary disappears, inspect exit versus break. If skipped rows are counted, inspect continue. If the tail is missing, check for an early whole-input read; if its final newline changes, forward it with cat rather than printf on a capture.

scenarios.title: Recover each delivery job independently
scenarios.summary: Choose the first ready source within a budget without abandoning other jobs or damaging failed outputs.
scenarios.objective: Arguments are LIMIT followed by 1–4 job IDs. LIMIT is exactly 1 or 2. Each ID is 1–8 characters: a–z first, then a–z, 0–9 or hyphens. For example, job scan uses scan.primary, scan.backup and scan.result. Process jobs in argument order, including repeats. For each valid ID, inspect ID.primary and then ID.backup, trying no more than LIMIT candidates. A candidate is usable only if its first line is exactly READY; an ending newline is optional, extra spaces or a carriage return are not. Copy the first usable candidate’s entire original content to ID.result, then print “Copied ID from primary.” or “Copied ID from backup.” on stdout. Do not try later candidates after success. If neither permitted candidate is usable, print “Unavailable: ID” on stderr and preserve its previous result (or keep it absent). Invalid IDs print “Invalid job: ID” on stderr and do not touch files. Continue other jobs; return 1 if any job failed, otherwise 0. Wrong argument count first gives “Usage: fallback LIMIT JOB...”; otherwise a bad LIMIT gives “Limit must be 1 or 2.” Both global errors return 2 with no stdout or file changes. Messages end in a newline. Preserve all source and unrelated files; successful jobs remain copied even if another job fails.

scenarios.explanation:
Follow the assignment’s policy at each boundary, then report the combined result. The reference below is one supported solution; equivalent behavior is accepted.

One supported solution, available on request:
valid_job() {
  case "$1" in
    ''|*[!a-z0-9-]*|?????????*) return 1 ;;
    [a-z]*) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}
copy_job() {
  local job="$1" limit="$2" attempt=0 source='' header='' found=1
  for side in primary backup; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if test "$attempt" -gt "$limit"; then break; fi
    source="$job.$side"
    if test -f "$source"; then
      header=''
      IFS= read -r header < "$source"
      if test "$header" = READY; then
        cat -- "$source" > "$job.result"
        printf 'Copied %s from %s.\n' "$job" "$side"
        found=0
        break
      fi
    fi
  done
  return "$found"
}
if test "$#" -lt 2 || test "$#" -gt 5; then
  printf 'Usage: fallback LIMIT JOB...\n' >&2
  exit 2
fi
case "$1" in
  1|2) limit="$1" ;;
  *) printf 'Limit must be 1 or 2.\n' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
shift
failed=0
for job in "$@"; do
  if valid_job "$job"; then
    if copy_job "$job" "$limit"; then
      true
    else
      printf 'Unavailable: %s\n' "$job" >&2
      failed=1
    fi
  else
    printf 'Invalid job: %s\n' "$job" >&2
    failed=1
    continue
  fi
done
exit "$failed"
hints: Validate argument count and the literal1|2 limit before shift or any file changes. Reject bad IDs before building source paths.
Put the candidate for loop inside a helper. Inspect .primary before .backup; clear header before each read and compare its text, not read status alone.
Open ID.result only after a ready header, copy with cat, then break that helper’s loop. Return the job result and preserve an independent caller failure flag.

No host commands/files/network or real timing. break/continue are portable shell concepts; this simulator supports only own-scope for/while loops, optional canonical ASCII counts 1–24, and no loop transfer through pipeline stages or caller functions/captures. Unimplemented syntax is an honest diagnostic. Flat UTF-8 virtual files only, bounded instructions/output/memory. No real locks, atomic rename, concurrent writers or crash recovery.

teaching.prerequisite_note: This capstone assumes the intake lesson, numeric validation, function return status and Bash local scope. Reopen those prerequisites if needed. Learn mode explains the first-success policy; Challenge keeps the same complete independent job assignment.

concepts.title: One failed job does not undo another
concepts.text: This task commits each successful job independently. Preserve the previous result of an unavailable job, report it and keep processing later jobs. This differs from the earlier all-or-nothing plan-publication tasks.

concepts.title: Bound the request before using it
concepts.text: Require a single-digit limit 1 or 2 before arithmetic. A job ID is 1–8 ordinary characters: a–z first, then a–z, 0–9 or hyphens. These exact characters are called ASCII; look-alikes are different. Reject a bad ID as one job failure before constructing a filename.

concepts.title: Investigate candidates in order
concepts.text: For a job, try its .primary file first and .backup second, within the limit. test -f checks virtual existence. Read the first line into a cleared header variable; only exact READY is usable. A final READY without a newline still supplies that header even when read returns1.

concepts.title: Choose before opening the destination
concepts.text: Read and check the header before redirecting output. Only a chosen candidate may replace JOB.result; cat copies its whole original text and line endings. An empty, missing or differently spelled header is not ready.

concepts.title: Stop the helper’s own loop
concepts.text: break ends the candidate loop after its first successful copy. It does not end the caller’s job loop. return reports the helper’s result. local keeps helper working variables separate and is Bash-specific; a portable helper with distinct variable names is also valid.

concepts.title: Keep the batch status
concepts.text: A job reports Copied or a specific error. Keep a separate overall failure flag and exit 1 if any job failed; a later success must not reset it. Handle repeated IDs as repeated requests in order. Never use exit inside the helper to abandon later jobs.

teaching.example:
choose_card() {
  local candidate='' header='' found=1
  for candidate in front-card reserve-card; do
    header=''
    IFS= read -r header < "$candidate"
    if test "$header" = AVAILABLE; then
      cat -- "$candidate" > gallery-card.txt
      printf 'Chosen: %s\n' "$candidate"
      found=0
      break
    fi
  done
  return "$found"
}
choose_card
teaching.inputs: Both practice card files start AVAILABLE and contain different text. The example chooses front-card and replaces only gallery-card.txt; no arguments are supplied. These names and the AVAILABLE marker differ from the assignment.
teaching.try_change: Remove the break line and Run example. Both choices are copied and the reserve text overwrites the first choice. Restore break to keep the first usable card.

scenarios.retry_guidance: If the backup overwrites a ready primary, inspect break or your done flag. If a failed result becomes empty, find an early > redirect. If later jobs disappear, inspect exit inside a helper. If only final READY files fail, check the stored header even when read returns1.
